g.text: Figure 2. The simplified donor pathway, drawn as the inference pass. Everything above the attention block is unchanged: one shared LSTM
reads the same 270-day window of 6 daily forcings and 30 static catchment attributes for all 531 basins and returns its last hidden state
h. Rows are basins throughout: blue rows are the 455 gauged basins of the fold, which form the fixed donor pool, and amber rows the 76
held-out ungauged basins. Queries supply Q and donors supply K; the self-diagonal of the logits is set to minus infinity in training and
in evaluation, so no basin attends to itself. What changes is the value. Instead of the donor hidden state plus a learned encoding of its
discharge, V is the donor's recent flow itself -- seven days of standardised log-flow anomaly, dimensionless and so transferable between
basins of very different size. There is no encoder MLP and no LayerNorm residual: the attended context c is the attention-weighted
regional flow anomaly over those same seven days, and it is concatenated to h_q rather than added to it, giving the head 263 inputs.
Dropout is applied to h_q alone and never to c, because a zeroed anomaly reads as flow sitting exactly at its long-term normal rather
than as missing data; for the same reason a donor is dropped from the softmax unless it reported on all seven days, and the per-day flag
bits of Figure 1 are gone. A two-layer MLP head emits flow in mm day-1. As before, at no stage does a query basin's own discharge, or any
statistic of it, enter the forward pass.
